links.comparator_used: Exhaustive manual review of all patients (simulated selective-review workflow ranked by uncertainty)
links.outcome: Proportion of patients needing expert review to capture all LLM extraction errors
links.effect: Complete error coverage by reviewing 8.3% of patients for hemiplegia, 8.2% for headache and 19.6% for seizure
links.tradeoff: Requires 15 LLM calls per model per patient (five temperatures x three repeats); seizure needed a larger review share (19.6%) than the other targets.
links.quote: Entropy-based triage achieved complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), and 19.6% for seizure.

links.comparator_used: No reliability scoring (correctly classified cases used as the reference)
links.outcome: Ability of consistency-based Shannon entropy across repeated calls to separate misclassified from correctly classified cases
links.effect: Entropy in misclassified cases was 2.4-3.4 times higher than in correctly classified cases
links.tradeoff: Requires 15 repeated calls per model per patient (five temperatures x three repeats).
links.quote: Entropy in misclassified cases was 2.4–3.4 times higher than in correctly classified cases.

links.comparator_used: Simulated uncertainty-ranked selective expert review vs reviewing more/all patients to achieve complete error coverage.
links.outcome: Expert-review workload needed to cover extraction errors.
links.effect: Complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), and 19.6% for seizure.
links.tradeoff: Still required expert review of the flagged subset: 8.3%, 8.2%, and 19.6% of patients for the reported targets.
links.quote: Entropy-based triage achieved complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), and 19.6% for seizure.
